svg.title: ACLs and segmentation: ordered rules, first match wins
svg.desc: Segments separate networks; routers let them talk; ACLs decide exactly which conversations are allowed
svg.text: ACLs and segmentation: ordered rules, first match wins
Segments separate networks; routers let them talk; ACLs decide exactly which conversations are allowed
TOPOLOGY · INTER-VLAN TRAFFIC CROSSES THE ROUTER
Top to bottom · first match wins · stop reading
A guest packet to the server hits rule 20 → DENIED. It never reaches rule 30.
WHERE AND WHICH WAY? — A RULE ON THE WRONG INTERFACE DOES NOTHING
(or it blocks the source from everything)
each packet judged alone; the reply is a
new packet that needs its own permit.
Order · direction · placement · implicit deny — the four things that decide what an ACL really does.
Segmentation (VLAN + subnet) creates the boundary; the ACL is the policy that says who may cross it.
